policy.name: Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility Admission Policy IRF-7 (synthetic)
policy.text: Admission to an inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) is medically necessary when ALL of the following are met at the time of admission: (1) a qualifying condition: stroke, spinal cord injury, brain injury, major multiple trauma, amputation, or hip fracture; (2) the patient requires active and ongoing intervention of at least two therapy disciplines, one of which must be physical or occupational therapy; (3) the patient is able and willing to participate in, and is expected to tolerate, an intensive rehabilitation program of at least 3 hours of therapy per day at least 5 days per week; (4) the patient is medically stable enough to participate in the intensive program and does not require acute hospital-level care; (5) measurable functional improvement is expected within a reasonable period, documented with a functional measure such as FIM; (6) a rehabilitation physician has completed a pre-admission screening within 48 hours before the requested admission date. Patients who cannot currently tolerate intensive therapy should be considered for a lower level of care and reassessed.

documents.name: IRF pre-auth request form
documents.text: Requested service: inpatient rehabilitation facility admission. Requested admission date: 2026-10-20. Expected length of stay: 14 days. Diagnosis: acute ischemic stroke, left MCA territory (I63.512), with right hemiparesis and aphasia. Referring: St. Clare Hospital, hospitalist service. Accepting rehabilitation physician: Dr. P. Sandoval, PM&R.

documents.name: Acute hospital H&P
documents.text: 71-year-old man brought in by EMS with right-sided weakness and word-finding difficulty. Last known well 2026-10-12 at 06:30. NIHSS 11. History: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation not on anticoagulation. Allergies: NKDA. Lives with wife in a two-story home; independent and driving before admission. Outside the thrombolysis window on arrival per stroke team.

documents.name: MRI brain report
documents.text: Acute infarct in the left middle cerebral artery territory involving the left frontal and parietal lobes and internal capsule. No hemorrhage. Chronic small vessel ischemic change.

documents.name: Neurology progress note
documents.text: Left MCA ischemic stroke. Per daughter, symptoms actually began the evening of 2026-10-11, with mild word-finding trouble before bed. Dense right arm weakness, right leg 3/5, expressive aphasia. Started apixaban for atrial fibrillation-related cardioembolic stroke. Recommend acute inpatient rehabilitation when medically ready.

documents.name: Physiatry pre-admission screen
documents.text: PM&R consult for IRF candidacy. Patient alert, follows commands, motivated. Currently able to tolerate 3 hours of therapy per day, 5 days per week. Requires physical therapy, occupational therapy and speech-language pathology. FIM motor 38, FIM cognition 18. Expected to improve to FIM motor approximately 60 within 14 days. Medically stable. Recommend IRF admission. OT evaluation reviewed.

documents.name: Hospitalist progress note
documents.text: New fever 38.6 C overnight, productive cough, SpO2 89% on room air. Chest X-ray: right lower lobe consolidation consistent with aspiration pneumonia. Started IV ampicillin-sulbactam and 2 L nasal cannula oxygen. Allergies: penicillin (rash). Hold therapy today.

documents.name: PT daily treatment log
documents.text: 2026-10-15: 60 minutes, gait training with hemi-walker. 2026-10-16: 0 minutes, held for fever. 2026-10-17: 20 minutes, session terminated for fatigue, SpO2 88% with exertion. 2026-10-18: 30 minutes, multiple rest breaks. 2026-10-19: 35 minutes, terminated early for fatigue. Patient willing and motivated but limited by endurance.

documents.name: SLP note
documents.text: Moderate oropharyngeal dysphagia; NPO except ice chips pending modified barium swallow study. Expressive aphasia, tolerated 15 minutes of language therapy before fatigue.

documents.name: Hospitalist progress note
documents.text: Day 4 of IV antibiotics. Tmax 37.9 C. Still requiring 1 L oxygen by nasal cannula. Lethargic in the afternoons. Not yet back to baseline. Continue IV antibiotics, plan transition to oral when afebrile for 24 hours.

documents.name: Physiatry re-evaluation addendum
documents.text: Re-evaluated after aspiration pneumonia. Currently tolerating 30 to 45 minutes of total therapy per day with frequent rest breaks. Unable to participate in 3 hours of therapy per day at this time. Rehabilitation potential remains good. Recommend SNF-level rehabilitation now, or reassess for IRF in 7 to 10 days if endurance improves.

documents.name: Case manager letter
documents.text: Patient clearly meets IRF criteria per the physiatry screen of 10/14 and family strongly prefers IRF over SNF. Please expedite approval so he can transfer 10/20. Note: the OT evaluation referenced in the physiatry screen is not attached to this packet, and the acute hospital discharge summary is pending.
